newsitem.title: USA: AeroThrust says dropped from lawsuits.
newsitem.headline: AeroThrust says dropped from lawsuits.

text.p: Celsius Industrier AB's AeroThrust Corp said Wednesday it has been dropped as a defendant in most lawsuits filed on behalf of the victims of ValuJet Inc's Flight 592 crash in the Everglades.

Kevin Boyd, a spokesman for AeroThrust, said the company remains named as a defendant in only "a handful" of other lawsuits among the 15 in which it were originally named. The company maintains it should not be held liable for the May accident since its only involvement with the plane was performing heavy maintenance on one of two United Technologies Corp Pratt & Whitney JT8D engines six months before.
The company said the lawyer for the plaintiffs in most of the cases, Aaron Podhurt, said he expected the few remaining lawsuits naming AeroThrust also would drop the company as a defendant.
AeroThrust President James McMillen said in a statement that federal investigators determined that both Pratt engines were operating at or near full power at the time of impact.
"It is unfortunate that we were named, and that our company's involvement in that accident was inaccurately described in the lawsuits, but this helps to clear the slate," McMillen said.
AeroThrust said ValuJet remains a client.
